alerts.title: DTG & Hyperglycemia Risk
alerts.message: Guidelines report hyperglycemia among previously non-diabetic adults on DTG. The patient has multiple risk factors for hyperglycemia: age ≥30, family history of DM, and BMI ≥25 kg/m². Since transitioning to DTG (TLD) 18 months ago, she has developed impaired fasting glucose (118 mg/dL) and HbA1c in the pre-diabetic range (6.1%), alongside significant weight gain and acanthosis nigricans. However, lifestyle factors and genetic predisposition are also potential contributors to this metabolic syndrome.

evidence.recommended_action: Do not initiate or transition to DTG if high glucose is present. For this patient already on DTG, monitor glucose every 3 months for the first year.

alerts.title: Missing DTG Glucose Monitoring
alerts.message: Guidelines specify glucose monitoring every 3 months for the first year for patients initiated on or transitioned to DTG. The patient transitioned to DTG 18 months ago, and there is no indication of regular glucose monitoring during that first year in the provided history. The current labs show new-onset impaired fasting glucose and pre-diabetes.

evidence.recommended_action: Establish a schedule for regular glucose monitoring as per guidelines for patients on DTG.

alerts.title: Obesity & Metabolic Syndrome
alerts.message: Obesity increases the risk of health problems like heart disease and diabetes. The patient's BMI has increased from 25.6 to 32.4 kg/m² (overweight to obese class I) since starting DTG, with a waist circumference of 96cm indicating central adiposity. She also has a dyslipidemia (high LDL, low HDL, high triglycerides) and new-onset elevated blood pressure. This constellation suggests a significant metabolic syndrome, which is a compounding risk factor for cardiovascular disease.

evidence.recommended_action: Address modifiable risk factors for obesity: counsel on healthy diet and physical activity.
